title: Customer EOS incident timeline (scratchpad)
content:
Purpose:
- Personal scratchpad capturing debugging breadcrumbs, commands tried, error snippets, hypotheses, and a draft internal + customer-facing timeline/comms for Customer EOS (acct: eos-inc).
- This is informal; will extract a clean timeline and status update for CS once we confirm root cause.

Quick summary:
- Customer reported intermittent 502/504s and corrupted streaming chunks when sending long-context requests (~12k tokens) to the hosted API model redwood-v2-7b (quantized variant) starting ~2026-03-01 21:00 UTC.
- Incidents spike correlated with a traffic surge from EOS (batch job at 20:45 UTC) that increased long-sequence requests to the hosted cluster in us-west.
- Initial mitigation: temporary rate-limit on EOS project, rolled back to redwood-v2-7b@2026-02-15 (previous build) for a canary, restarted affected worker pool. Errors reduced but not eliminated.

Raw timeline (notes + timestamps):
- 2026-03-01 20:46 UTC: EOS starts batch inference (customer reported). Observed 2x baseline long-seq QPS on us-west-hosted.
- 2026-03-01 21:02 UTC: First slack alert - increased 502s from hosted-api-prod-usw.
- 2026-03-01 21:05 UTC: Pager on-call (Noah) joins, initial hypothesis: autoscaler or upstream load balancer.
- 2026-03-01 21:12 UTC: Logs from hosted-api-prod show repeated:
  - "error: failed to stream response: broken pipe"
  - "kv_cache: prefix miss, fallback to full recompute"
  - "worker pod dedicated-pool-3-7fdb: segmentation fault (signal 11)"
- 2026-03-01 21:20 UTC: Repro attempt with curl against redwood-v2-7b (long prompt >10k tokens):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-v2-7b","prompt":"<~12k token prompt>","max_tokens":1024}'
  -> Response: HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
  -> Body excerpt: "stream_error: upstream closed connection before EOS"
- 2026-03-01 21:28 UTC: Attempted local repro by running serving-runtime in debug with same quantized model on staging GPU (a40):
  ./bazel-bin/serving/runtime --model-path=/models/rw-v2-7b-q8 --port=8080 --log=debug
  Observed repeated OOMs in logs then segfaults. Partial stack:
  "libc.so.6(+0x3c920) [0x7f4b8c1b3920]"
  "serving::kv_cache::get_prefix(...) at kv_cache.cc:214"
- 2026-03-01 21:40 UTC: Hypothesis: quantized kernel change in latest build (2026-02-26) causes unstable memory access under heavy long-seq loads -> leads to segfault and connection closes. Also possible garbage in prefix cache when used concurrently across multiple requests.
- 2026-03-01 21:50 UTC: Rollback attempt: shift EOS traffic to redwood-v2-7b@2026-02-15 (older build) via routing rule. Immediate drop in 502s for 10 minutes.
- 2026-03-01 22:05 UTC: Small number of 502s reappear. Investigating shared infra (LB / proxy) by checking envoy traces — traces show worker returning 500 then closing stream mid-chunk.
- 2026-03-01 22:30 UTC: Restarted dedicated-pool-3 (3 pods). After restart, error rate dropped to near-zero for ~30 minutes.
- 2026-03-01 23:05 UTC: One pod crash observed again; crash logs show memory corruption address 0x7fffe...
- 2026-03-02 00:10 UTC: Escalated to Applied ML / Runtime (Ava + Linda). Ava reproduced segfault with ASAN enabled on staging, confirms heap-buffer-overflow in kv_cache.cc:214 when handling >8k prefix + continuous streaming calls.
- 2026-03-02 03:00 UTC: Temporary mitigation: disabled prefix caching for quantized models in hosted-prod-usw via feature flag roll-out. Monitoring.
- 2026-03-02 04:20 UTC: Error rates fall to baseline. Customer reports improved behavior but asks for root cause and timeline.

Commands tried (for reproducibility):
- curl repro (production token masked):
  curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-v2-7b","prompt":"<long prompt>","stream":true}'
- Local debug run (staging):
  ./bazel-bin/serving/runtime --model-path=/models/rw-v2-7b-q8 --enable-asan --log=debug
- Heap/ASAN repro steps:
  1) Load model quantized q8 build 2026-02-26
  2) Send 12k token prompt repeatedly (concurrent 8 workers)
  3) Observe ASAN report: heap-buffer-overflow in kv_cache.cc:214
- Envoy/proxy trace command:
  curl -s 'http://envoy-admin.local/traces?request_id=abc123'
- Pod logs snippet retrieval:
  kubectl -n hosted-prod logs dedicated-pool-3-7fdb --since=2h --tail=500

Key error snippets (copied):
- "stream_error: upstream closed connection before EOS"
- "segmentation fault (signal 11) at 0x7f4b8c1b3920"
- ASAN excerpt: "==2468==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow on address 0x60200000b7f0 at pc 0x7f8c1234"
- serving log: "kv_cache.cc:214: attempt to read 512 bytes past buffer end"

Hypotheses (ordered by likelihood):
1) Regression introduced in quantized kernel or kv_cache race condition (since ASAN repro points to kv_cache.cc). Concurrency path with long-prefix + streaming triggers overflow.
2) Autoscaler/proxy amplified the failure mode by sending too many concurrent long-seq requests to same worker, exposing the race.
3) Unrelated hardware fault (unlikely given ASAN reproduces locally with same binary)

Mitigations taken:
- Immediate: rate-limited EOS project long-context requests at 2026-03-01 22:00 UTC.
- Rollback: routed EOS to older model build 2026-02-15 as canary; helped temporarily.
- Restarted worker pool dedicated-pool-3.
- Feature-flagged off prefix caching for quantized models in hosted-prod-usw (temporary until fix merged).

Next steps (owner tags):
- eng-serv-runtime (Ava): root-cause PR with ASAN fix for kv_cache bounds check. Target: 2026-03-04. (owner: Ava Ramirez)
- eng-release (Noah): coordinate patch rollout cadence + canary tests (owner: Noah Thompson)
- sre/infra (Linda): add a probe to detect repeated segfaults and auto-schedule pod replacement/backoff (owner: Linda Cho)
- CS (me/Ryan): draft customer-facing timeline and post-mortem once fix validated.

Draft internal blurb (for #incident or triage doc):
- TL;DR: Quantized model prefix cache bug caused heap corruption under concurrent long-prefix streaming requests, resulting in segfaults and upstream stream closures (502/504). Temporary mitigations reduced errors; runtime team is preparing an ASAN-backed patch. Next update after fix validated in canary (~24-48h).

Draft customer-facing message (short):
Hi Alice,

Thanks for the report and for the patience. We identified a bug in the runtime's prefix cache when used with the quantized redwood-v2-7b build. Under high concurrency with very long prompts we saw memory corruption that caused pods to crash and streams to terminate prematurely. We have:
- applied a temporary mitigation (disabled prefix caching for quantized models in the affected region)
- rolled back your traffic to a stable build while we test a fix
- prioritized a fix; runtime team has an ASAN-validated patch and will rollout to canary in the next 24 hours

We’ll follow up with a full root cause and timeline once the change is validated. If you need a direct point of contact for urgent items, reply to this thread and I’ll connect you to our SRE lead. — Ryan

Notes / meta:
- Linked artifacts: JIRA-4821 (INC), CONFLUENCE-8901 (incident runbook), PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/512
- Collabs: pinged Ava, Noah, Linda. Need to add Dominic from infra if we broaden the probe.
- Keep this doc as scratch until we have the fix validated; then produce cleaned timeline and post-mortem.
